_README: THE EQUIVALENCE CLASSIFICATION — MUTATION-EQUIVALENCE-2026-08-04 §5/§6.1.
A surviving mutant is not automatically a test gap. Some cannot be killed by ANY input: `if (lo < 0)
lo = 0` mutated to `<=` still assigns 0 when lo IS 0. Reporting those against a `killed / tested`
denominator makes the target unreachable by arithmetic and buries the real gaps among them.
Until now this classification lived in BRIEF PROSE, which means every sweep re-litigated the same
survivors and no tool could report it. This file is that prose made machine-readable, and it is
consumed by `tools/mutate.mjs` (see `classifySurvivors`) so a run reports `killed / distinguishable`
beside the raw rate rather than instead of it.
MATCHED ON (line, op, before, after) — `survivorKey` in `tools/mutate.mjs`, the one key the classifier,
the recorded-selection path and `findCanary` all use. `after` IS part of the key: one source line can
carry several mutants of one operator, and (line, op, before) alone would collapse them into one entry.
An entry that omits `after` reads as the empty string (`m.after ?? ''`). Rewording an operator's output
text therefore DOES orphan the entries it produced: re-record them.
THE CLASSES, and they are not interchangeable:
· no-distinguishing-input  — a battery of inputs was run against original and mutant and every
one produced byte-identical output. STRONG EVIDENCE, NOT PROOF: a
proof needs an argument over the whole input domain. `probe` records
what was actually run, so the claim can be re-checked or widened.
· untestable-by-design     — a log string, or a branch unreachable by construction. The argument
goes in `why` and must be about the CODE, not about the test suite.
· equivalent               — PROVEN identical: original and mutant compute the same function,
not merely agreed on every input tried. Stronger than
no-distinguishing-input, and it excuses for the same reason.
ABSENT from this list and from EXCUSING until 2026-09-07, so an
`equivalent` entry was reported as a REAL GAP — a TODO to write a
test for a mutant carrying a proof that no such test exists.
Upgrading an entry to it made the classification WEAKER. Fixed
and pinned in both directions.
· real-gap                 — killable, no test yet. These stay in the distinguishable denominator;
they are debt, not equivalence. An entry here is a TODO, not an excuse.
THIS FILE CANNOT FLATTER A RATE, BY CONSTRUCTION. `mutate.mjs` reports three failure modes loudly:
· REFUTED  — an entry claims equivalence and the mutant was KILLED. The classification is WRONG;
a distinguishing input exists after all. Fix the entry, never the test.
· ORPHANED — an entry matches no generated mutant (the line moved, or the code changed). It is
excluded from every count until re-verified, so a stale entry shrinks nothing.
· unclassified survivors are counted and named, so silence is never mistaken for equivalence.
Only `no-distinguishing-input` and `untestable-by-design` leave the denominator. `real-gap` does not.
A RE-ANCHOR MOVES `line` AND NOTHING ELSE. `tools/reanchor-equivalence.mjs --probe --write` moves an
entry whose (op, before) still matches exactly ONE generated mutant, and it refuses to move any entry
without a probe (owner ruling, board #1549 item 21, 2026-10-26). The probe re-runs that mutant at its
NEW address through `mutate.mjs --only`: a KILL refutes an excusing entry, which then keeps its
orphaned address, and only a survivor earns the move. The `reanchored` field records the move — `at`,
`from`, `commit`, `outcome`, and the groups the probe ran. It records the ADDRESS, never the claim:
`why` and `probe` hold the equivalence argument and no re-anchor touches either.
THE OPTIONAL `fn` QUALIFIER (2026-10-26, residue
2026-10-26-a-line-keyed-equivalence-entry-that-drifts-ambiguously-cannot-be-placed).
The four-field key above is keyed on a LINE, so any edit ABOVE a recorded mutant detaches its entry
and the gate goes back to blocking a survivor somebody already classified. By 2026-10-26 that had
happened to 168 of 434 entries. An entry may therefore also carry `fn`, the name of the enclosing
named function, and an entry that carries one is addressed by (fn, op, before, after) with the line
ignored — so it survives an edit above it, and detaches only when the mutation leaves that function,
which is a different site and should detach.
`fn` is OPTIONAL and an absent one constrains nothing: an entry without it is matched on its line,
exactly as every entry recorded before that date is. Two conditions govern writing one, and
`tools/reanchor-equivalence.mjs --qualify` enforces both rather than trusting an author: the entry
must already be exactly anchored, so the qualifier records where it already points and moves no
address; and its (fn, op, before, after) identity must be UNIQUE among the file’s mutants, or the
line-free match would widen one excuse onto a sibling mutant nobody probed. 4 entries in
oxydex-dsp.js fail the second test and stay line-keyed. A mutant outside any named function cannot
carry a qualifier at all; `enclosingFn` answers null there and the line is the only address it has.
Never hand-write `fn`. The enclosing function is stamped on every mutant by
`mutate.mjs --dry-run --json`, the one process that holds the source, so no sibling tool re-derives
it and drifts.
